photo.title: Sitting out place with Sekrengi bamboos around
Resting place in the rice fields at Konoma

Large group standing in village clearing, and in the foreground is a group of two men and four women who appear to be wearing high status or ceremonial dress. The men are wearing rectangular chest ornaments with rows of cowrie shells alternating with short goat hair fringes and long goat hair fringes round the edges, with a neck strap with cowrie shells and a long goat hair fringe. The men are also wearing bead necklaces with several strands. One of the men is wearing a black kilt with three rows of cowrie shells, and has a thick ivory armlet on each arm, indicating high status. Both men are wearing smaller brass armlets and beaded ear ornaments. One of the women is wearing a dark body cloth with white stripes, a bead necklace with several strands and large brass rings in her ears. The other three women, all of whom have shaven hair, are wearing white body cloths with black and white stripes, bead necklaces and large brass earrings which they have flipped upwards.  Behind the group is an elevated stone platform, and on it are four large baskets with conical lids and a fabric sack with carrying strap and a folded cane chair bound with straps. Behind the platform is a stone terrace, on which most of the group is standing. Individuals in the group are holding containers such as a folded leaf, a small basket, pottery vessel and a bamboo water vessel.

'Resopu / Angami' (handwritten caption). Bust portrait of an Angami Naga man named Resopu, wearing ear ornaments and a striped white cloak over a waistcoat with lapels, holding a flower. 'I only heard yesterday of the death of Resopu, perhaps the best of all my dobashis [interpreters], in Cheswejuma of pneumonia.' - Hutton, tour diary, 20 January 1922

'Angami / House horns, Kigwema' (handwritten caption). View of the roof of a house in the Angami Naga village of Kigwema, with roof-horns, carved with holes and spikes and perching birds, projecting from the front rafters.

'Angami. / Resopu'  (handwritten caption). Bust portrait of an Angami Naga man named Resopu, wearing ear ornaments and a striped white cloak over a waistcoat with lapels, holding a flower. 'I only heard yesterday of the death of Resopu, perhaps the best of all my dobashis [interpreters], in Cheswejuma of pneumonia.' - Hutton, tour diary, 20 January 1922

'Kigwema' (handwritten caption). View of the roof of a house in the Angami Naga village of Kigwema, with roof-horns, carved with holes and spikes and perching birds, projecting from the front rafters.

'Monoliths at Khezabama / Angami 1921' (handwritten caption). View of a Naga man, wearing ear ornaments, necklaces, a cloak, and a striped apron, standing by one of an irregular line of monoliths on flat ground at the bottom of a short steep slope into which paths have been cut, at the village of Khezabama/Khizabama (now Chizami).
Half-length portrait of an Angami Naga woman from Khonoma, wearing bracelets, many necklaces, and a striped cloak, identified as Wüsezowü, possibly of the Semoma subgroup.

'Angami / Memi types from Sopvomi' (handwritten caption). Three-quarter-length portrait of four Angami Naga men of the Memi group, from Sopvomi (possibly = Sopvoma = Mao), wearing cloaks and necklaces.

'Angami / Memi types from Sopvomi' (handwritten caption). Bust portrait from the side of two Angami Naga men of the Memi group, from Sopvomi (possibly = Sopvoma = Mao), showing distinctive ear ornaments.

'Angami. / Khonoma _ _ of the Thevoma and Semoma khels.' (handwritten caption). View from a nearby hill of a hillside road to hilltop settlements at Khonoma of the Thevoma and Semoma khels (clans) of the Angami Naga people.

'Angami. / THEPFUVITSE of Khonoma.' (handwritten caption). Full-length portrait of an Angami Naga man identified as Thepfuvitse of Khonoma (who worked as an interpreter for J. H. Hutton), standing by a trellis in a garden, wearing ear ornaments, beaded bands and a key on a chain around his neck, a European-style waistcoat, a striped skirt, a striped cloak over his shoulder, and bangles at his knees.

'Angami. / Thepfuyugur of Mezoma & Thepfuvitsu (?) of Khonoma' (handwritten caption). Bust profile portrait from the left side of two Angami Naga men, identified as Thepfuyugur of Mezoma (left) and Thepfuvitsu of Khonoma (who worked for J. H. Hutton as an interpreter, right), both wearing ear ornaments and necklaces, Thepfuyugur with an elaborate hair fastening, Thepfuvitsu with a simple pigtail.

'Angami / Memi types from Sopvomi' (handwritten caption). Bust portrait from behind of two Angami Naga men of the Memi group, from Sopvomi (possibly = Sopvoma = Mao), showing necklaces and distinctive ear ornaments.

View of an Angami Naga woman's grave surmounted with a wooden frame, within which are baskets, other woven objects, and unspun cotton, behind which are visible the legs of several people wearing cloaks and bangles or bindings at the knee.

'The chicken released on the male stone' (handwritten caption). View of a small fowl standing on a large 'male' stone harnessed with creeper ropes, as part of an Angami Naga stone-erecting ceremony called 'kechiesü', with spectators behind.
